refreshes.notes: Nineteen minors, purely additive: 200 members -> 210, nothing withdrawn. The six changed operations all gained parameters — `metadata` on add_friends and create_api_friend, `joinRequired` on create_api_tournament, `party_update` on create_envelope_message, all optional; create_party_create_message and create_party_message gained `label`/`hidden` as required. The go/no-go verdict is unmoved: decision stays no-go and the missing-member set (12 API* enum constants plus six client-lifecycle names) is byte-identical to the v3.21.1 measurement, so the additions expand the emitted surface without covering anything the authored fork owns. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (830 type tokens, 0 unknown), so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged. The fragile `proto` source path into upstream's Go vendor/ tree survived the bump and was re-verified at v3.40.0 before fetching. staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history and nothing is committed between checkpoints, so 19 intermediate fetches would multiply the work without adding an isolation point. changedMembers and these notes are unchecked prose — the committed guard reads addedMembers and removedMembers only.

Two minors plus a patch (1.2.5 -> 1.3.1), net additive: 809 members -> 839, three withdrawn. The removals are one rework, not a deprecation: druid.instance._input_blacklist and _input_whitelist collapse into the single _input_filter field plus the new input_filter.blacklist/whitelist pair, and druid.scroll._on_mouse_hover went away with it. New public API arrives on progress (get_value/set_value), swipe (is_enabled/set_enabled), timer (set_value), rich_text (set_justify/is_justify), drag (add_drag_action/remove_drag_action/hover), data_list (refresh), input (get_text_visual) and the module function get_druid; the druid.button.style constants are now surfaced as fields. Seven declarations changed. Two break a call site a consumer wrote: druid.text.set_text went from set_text(): void to set_text(new_text: string): druid_text, so a written text:set_text() now fails on a missing required argument, and druid.button.style went from LuaTable to the all-optional druid_button_style, so a value typed LuaTable no longer assigns to it. Four widen what a consumer may pass, so existing call sites still compile: get_widget gained a trailing optional template parameter, which moved the docs-site emitter-equivalence assertion with it; druid.instance.set_whitelist and druid.instance.set_blacklist made their one required parameter optional; and druid.button.init widened its callback from () => void to (self, custom_args, button_instance) => void, which a zero-parameter callback still satisfies. One is private: druid.drag._on_touch_release dropped its leading action_id: Hash parameter. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (0 unknown), so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged, and every annotationOverrides key still resolved against the new fixtures (applyAnnotationOverrides throws on an absent key, so the emit pass proves it). staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history, so intermediate fetches would add work without an isolation point. Pinned at tag 1.3.1 rather than the 1.3.0 release because upstream:library-check ranks tags by commit date and 1.3.1 is the newest. What this guard can witness is directional: a removedMembers name still emitted, or an addedMembers name not emitted at all. A member present at BOTH refs but listed under addedMembers would pass, because the 1.2.5 fixture bytes do not survive this commit. changedMembers and these notes are unchecked prose - the committed guard reads addedMembers and removedMembers only.

Two majors (4 -> 6), the largest jump in this backlog: 135 members -> 153, two withdrawn, and both withdrawals were emitted in the shipped .d.ts at 4, so both break a consumer call site. `decore.event_bus.process_all` is gone because upstream folded it into `process`, which now takes an entity-aware callback and returns LuaMultiReturn<[events, entities]> instead of one list; `system.nocache` is gone with the tiny-ecs rework that replaced the no-cache opt-out with a shape cache (tiny_ecs.setShapeValidation, tiny_ecs.bumpShapeCache, world.shapeGeneration, world.shapeSystems, entity.__shape, system.hasOnModify are its new surface). The event bus gained entity-parallel storage (event_entities, stash_entities, get_event_entities, get_stash_entities) and widened its keys from `string` to `string | Hash`; `get_events` also changed from a nullary `(): void` to `(event_name): unknown[] | undefined`, so the old declaration was wrong about its own arity. Elsewhere: a new `remove_component` module function, an `out` buffer on the find-entities pair, per-phase system lists on `world` (systemsUpdate, systemsPreWrap, systemsPostWrap, systemsLateUpdate, systemsFixedUpdate, systemsOnModify) plus world.event and world.id_to_entity, and system.decore.register_with_parent. That `out` buffer arrives asymmetrically: the module-level `find_entities` takes it as a trailing optional parameter, while the same buffer on the `world.findEntities` field is a required fourth parameter, so a three-argument call through the field stops compiling. The cause is that a nilable parameter annotated inside a `fun(...)` field is not lowered to `?`, which the untouched `component_value: unknown | undefined` on the same emitted line already demonstrates at both refs. Six of the twelve changed declarations break a call site a consumer wrote, and two of those break silently. `decore.event_bus.trigger` moved from `(event_name, data)` to `(event_name, entity?, data?)`, inserting `entity` ahead of the payload - the delta's one silent break for an ordinary payload, because the emitted `entity` interface is all-optional (id, prefab_id, pack_id, parent_prefab_id, child_instancies, parent_id, children_ids, __shape), so a payload variable sharing any one of those keys satisfies TypeScript's weak-type check, compiles, and binds to the entity slot at runtime. The boundary is narrower than that reads: a fresh object literal carrying a key outside that set is still caught by excess-property checking, so the silent path is a non-fresh payload, or a literal whose keys all happen to be entity keys. `decore.event_bus.set_merge_policy` and `decore.event_bus.merge_callbacks` both re-shaped the merge callback from `(new_event, events, entity_map)` to `(entity, data, datas, entity_map)`; an inline arrow callback re-binds contextually with no error, so every parameter name in an existing body now lies about what it holds - the second silent break. The remaining breaks are loud: `process`'s callback moved from `(events)` / `(context, events)` to `(entity, data)` / `(context, entity, data)`, alongside the LuaMultiReturn return recorded above; a written `get_events()` no longer compiles now that the event name is required; `get_stash`'s elements moved from `LuaTable` to `unknown`, so using one as a table needs a cast; and the four `LuaTable` fields widened their key from `string` to `string | Hash` (with events_by_entity and stash_by_entity widening their inner key from `entity` to `entity | string`), so an explicit `LuaTable<string, ...>` annotation over them no longer assigns. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (0 unknown, 204 type tokens), so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged. `--fetch` has no per-target filter and re-downloaded all 13 LuaLS targets; only fixtures/luals/decore/ moved, which confirms the other twelve tag pins are byte-stable. staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history, so an intermediate fetch at 5 would add work without an isolation point. What this guard can witness is directional: a removedMembers name still emitted, or an addedMembers name not emitted at all. changedMembers and these notes are unchecked prose - the committed guard reads addedMembers and removedMembers only.

Two tags (19 -> 21) for the smallest delta in this backlog: of the five committed fixture files only event/promise.lua moved, and the model surface went 61 members -> 62 with one addition and no withdrawal. The one addition is `promise.on_cancel`, which upstream promoted to a public field on the promise class. That promotion has a second half the guard cannot witness: the same release re-annotated `cancellation` as `---@field private`, so `isPublicField` now hides it and the shipped surface swapped `cancellation: promise_cancelled_context` for `on_cancel: event` in both generated/event.d.ts and api-doc/event.json. That breaks a consumer who read `my_promise.cancellation`; the replacement is `my_promise.on_cancel`, the same underlying event object upstream previously reached only through `cancellation.on_cancel`. `removedMembers` is empty by construction rather than by observation: buildTargetModel — the guard's member source — retains members of every visibility and only the emit, api-doc and fidelity passes apply isPublicField, so naming `promise.cancellation` here would red the guard against a member the model still yields. `promise:cancel()` also changed behavior without changing arity: a settled promise is now left as-is instead of running _cancel_promise(), and only pending descendants are rejected. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (0 unknown, 85 type tokens) and fidelity/event.json is byte-unchanged, so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged. `--fetch` has no per-target filter and re-downloaded all 13 LuaLS targets; only fixtures/luals/event/ moved, which confirms the other twelve tag pins are byte-stable. Tags are bare integers, so 21 was resolved as the highest integer rather than the highest string, where 9 would outrank it. staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history, so an intermediate fetch at 20 would add work without an isolation point. What this guard can witness is directional: a removedMembers name still emitted, or an addedMembers name not emitted at all. changedMembers and these notes are unchecked prose - the committed guard reads addedMembers and removedMembers only.

Bare integer tags, so 7 was resolved as the highest integer rather than the highest string, where 6 would outrank it. Upstream restructured the library at 7: log/log.lua shrank to a facade and three new files appeared under log/internal/ (config.lua, file_writer.lua, formatter.lua), all matched by the existing `log/**/*.lua` sourceGlobs, so the intake needed no config change and the `debuginfo` typeRename is still live — internal/formatter.lua and internal/file_writer.lua both still annotate that type. The model surface went 14 members -> 20. Eight additions are the new file-output API (`set_file`, `get_file`, `clear_log_files`, `final`, and the per-logger `log.set_file_nearby`) plus a custom-handler API (`add_callback`, `remove_callback`, `clear_callbacks`). Two withdrawals: `get_default_logger_name` moved out of the public module into internal/formatter.lua, and `log.format` is gone from the logger class. `get_default_logger_name` is the consumer-visible break — it was declared in generated/log.d.ts at 6, so a project calling log.get_default_logger_name() must move, and there is no public replacement since the default name is now derived internally. `log.format` was never emitted at 6 (buildTargetModel yields members of every visibility while the emit pass applies isPublicField), so its withdrawal reaches no consumer. Three changes the name lists cannot witness: the five level methods (`trace`/`debug`/`info`/`warn`/`error`) widened their `message` parameter from `string` to `string | undefined`, which is safe for every existing call site; `_last_gc_memory` and `_last_message_time` were model-only at 6 and are now emitted as optional fields; and the `log` class gained a class-level `@overload`, which the emitter lowered into a call signature on `interface log`. That `@overload` describes the module table, not the logger instance: upstream reuses `M` as both, but only the module table receives `__call` (`return setmetatable(M, { __call = ... })`), while `get_logger` hands back `setmetatable(instance, METATABLE)` over `local METATABLE = { __index = M }`. Lua reads `__call` raw off the value's own metatable, so a logger is not callable and `log.get_logger(name)(sub)` would type-check and then die at runtime attempting to call a table value. The signature is therefore dropped from the emitted surface with an `annotationOverrides` `callSignature` entry, and `changedMembers` still lists `log.log` for the unrelated `@local` method. The bare `log` namespace gains nothing colliding with the Lua standard library — lua-types declares no `log` global, and every new name lands inside `declare module 'log.log'`. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (0 unknown, 9 -> 18 members and 18 -> 25 type tokens), so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged and `bun run fidelity:floor` is a no-op. `--fetch` has no per-target filter and re-downloaded all 13 LuaLS targets; only fixtures/luals/log/ moved, which confirms the other twelve pins are byte-stable. staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history, so an intermediate fetch at an in-between tag would add work without an isolation point. What this guard can witness is directional: a removedMembers name still emitted, or an addedMembers name not emitted at all. changedMembers and these notes are unchecked prose - the committed guard reads addedMembers and removedMembers only.

runtime.8 -> runtime.10, purely additive: 90 members -> 118, none withdrawn and no existing declaration changed (the emitted panthera.d.ts diff has zero deleted lines). Resolved inside the runtime.* tag family deliberately: the repository's newest tag overall is editor.1254, an editor release whose sources are not the runtime this target pins, so ranking tags by recency alone would have fetched the wrong tree. The sourceGlobs (panthera/**/*.lua) still select at the new ref -- the fixture directory holds 4 files, 2 of which moved -- so the empty-selection failure mode, which would have yielded a silently thinner surface rather than an error, did not occur. --fetch has no per-target filter, so this re-downloaded all 13 LuaLS targets; every fixture outside fixtures/luals/panthera/ came back byte-stable at its unchanged ref. The new surface is the clip and collect-buffer machinery the release introduced: three new interfaces (panthera_collect_context, panthera_collect_buffer, panthera_animation_state_value), six new fields on panthera_animation (clips, template_states, collect_buffer, play_animation, play_options, play_sample_depth), group_animation_order on the animation data, and five internal helpers that reach the .d.ts (_local_speed, _playback_speed, _find_animation, _animation_log_data, _log_missing_animation). Four further added names -- _create_clip_state, _start_playback, _update_clips and start_animation_key -- are in buildTargetModel but the emitter filters them out of the .d.ts; they are listed because this guard reads the model, not the emitted file. Three already-declared members were reworded upstream with no signature change: play gained a sentence about the single driving timer, and the childs and timer_id field docs were rewritten, but all three declarations are byte-identical across the move, so changedMembers is empty and no consumer call site is affected. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (0 unknown) with undocumentedMembers 30 -> 38, so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged -- the only movement that floor could have shown is a drop, which would have been a finding rather than a floor to hand-edit. staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history, so intermediate fetches would add work without an isolation point. One minor (v2.0.0 -> v2.1.0), purely additive: 81 members -> 85, none withdrawn, and the emitted bridge.d.ts diff has zero deleted lines, so no existing declaration changed and changedMembers is empty. The whole delta is one new sub-namespace, bridge.notifications, wrapping the platform's leave-the-game notification API: is_supported, schedule (a { id, title, description, delaySeconds, image, callToAction, payload } table whose launch payload is read back through the existing bridge.platform.payload), cancel by id, and cancel_all. Bridge is the only script_api target and the only refreshed library with a published `exports` entry (`./bridge.bridge`), so these names reach a consumer who imports the declarations directly rather than through resolve alone; nothing they already import moved. The `scriptApi` source path bridge/api/bridge.script_api was re-verified at v2.1.0 before fetching -- fetchScriptApiFixture writes whatever the raw URL returns, so a moved path would have written a 404 body into the fixture instead of failing. The nested-namespace flatten hazard did not fire: emitScriptApiDeclaration keeps one level of sub-namespace, and the release adds a 14th sibling at the existing depth rather than a second nesting level, so nothing collapsed silently. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (0 unknown, 81 -> 85 members and 135 -> 144 type tokens, undocumentedMembers still 0), so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged and no new type token needed a resolver mapping. The script_api lane has a single target, so --fetch moved only this fixture and there is no sibling pin to confirm byte-stable. staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history, so an intermediate fetch would add work without an isolation point.
